issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream changes the contract callers rely on without spec update
issues.detail: The JSONTranslator middleware now reads from req.bounded_stream instead of req.stream. These are not substitutable: bounded_stream enforces Content-Length and may return empty bytes when stream would block or raise. The contract change is silent — no docstring, no versionchanged directive, no comment explaining why. Callers downstream of the middleware now see different behavior on malformed Content-Length.

issues.description: FAQ example handler violates its own implicit contract by reading req.content_length bytes without bound check
issues.detail: PostTest.on_post calls req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0) with a client-supplied length. The handler's postcondition (return 400 on empty-but-claimed body) is fine, but the precondition is unstated: an attacker-supplied Content-Length of GB triggers unbounded allocation. A documentation example becomes a copy-paste foot-gun. State the bound in the spec or use bounded_stream.

issues.description: README diff reorders StorageError.handle parameters, breaking the documented error-handler ADT
issues.detail: The README snippet changes handle(ex, req, resp, params) to handle(req, resp, ex, params). Falcon's error_handler contract has a specific signature; if the README now shows the new signature while leaving the rest of the example consistent with older Falcon, readers copying this code hit an LSP-style substitution failure against the framework's expected callable shape. Verify against current add_error_handler contract.

issues.description: New POST tests assert behavior without naming the contract being tested
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 assertions check status codes but the test has no docstring stating which invariant of things_advanced is under test (auth + JSON + body-required contract). Future maintainers reading a failure will not know whether the 400 is the spec or an accident. Add a one-line spec comment per assertion block.

issues.description: FAQ does not specify the contract difference between stream and bounded_stream that motivated the example
issues.detail: The new FAQ section teaches how to override headers but does not state the underlying ADT distinction: stream is the raw WSGI input (no Content-Length enforcement), bounded_stream guarantees reads respect Content-Length. Without that contract statement, readers will not understand why the example's example example reproduces the bug. Add one paragraph naming the invariant.

review.summary: The PR adds useful regression tests but quietly changes a contract: req.stream becomes req.bounded_stream in the JSONTranslator middleware, which is not a clean substitution and is not documented with a versionchanged note or comment. The FAQ example, while pedagogically useful, omits the underlying ADT distinction between stream and bounded_stream — exactly the invariant that makes the test meaningful — and contains an unbounded read pattern that callers will copy. The README parameter reorder for StorageError.handle should be verified against Falcon's current error-handler signature. Tests should name the contract they enforce. None of these block merge on correctness grounds, but the spec discipline is thin for a change that touches a middleware contract.
